aiReadyLines.text: 38 ENGLISH FOR TODAY
Students : Wrong thing.
Then your conscience will tell you, “This is a wrong thing. You must
not do it.” If you steal or do a bad thing, your conscience will prick
you and trouble you. And you will never have your peace of mind.
So, to be a good and happy person, you should have a clear conscience.
Tick the best answers to the following multiple choice questions.
“The students are confused.” The underlined words mean they
can think clearly.
cannot understand.
are unable to speak.
When you buy a thing from a Morality Shop, you
pay the money to the office.
pay the money later.
keep the money in the shop.
A person with a clear conscience
usually does the wrong thing.
always gets confused.
always does the right thing.
in pairs. Ask and answer the following questions.
What are the advantages and disadvantages of a morality shop?
What kind of shop will you prefer—a fixed price shop or a morality shop?
In groups or pairs, discuss and choose the best answer to this question.
Then say why you have chosen that answer.
Suppose, you are alone in the school yard. Suddenly you find a hundred-taka
note lying on the ground. What will you do?
pick up the money and hand over it to the Head Teacher.
pick up the money and quickly put it in my pocket.
leave the note where it is lying.
D Discuss in groups and write an answer to this question.
Is it possible to open a Morality Shop in your school?
You may discuss the following points / issues:
permission, things / items,
money / fund, how to prevent stealing

38 ENGLISH FOR TODAY
Students : Wrong thing.
Then your conscience will tell you, “This is a wrong thing. You must
not do it.” If you steal or do a bad thing, your conscience will prick
you and trouble you. And you will never have your peace of mind.
So, to be a good and happy person, you should have a clear conscience.
Tick the best answers to the following multiple choice questions.
1. “The students are confused.” The underlined words mean they
a. can think clearly.
b. cannot understand.
c. are unable to speak.
2. When you buy a thing from a Morality Shop, you
a. pay the money to the office.
b. pay the money later.
c. keep the money in the shop.
3. A person with a clear conscience
a. usually does the wrong thing.
b. always gets confused.
c. always does the right thing.
B. in pairs. Ask and answer the following questions.
a. What are the advantages and disadvantages of a morality shop?
b. What kind of shop will you prefer—a fixed price shop or a morality shop?
Cc. In groups or pairs, discuss and choose the best answer to this question.
Then say why you have chosen that answer.
Suppose, you are alone in the school yard. Suddenly you find a hundred-taka
note lying on the ground. What will you do?
I will
a. pick up the money and hand over it to the Head Teacher.
b. pick up the money and quickly put it in my pocket.
c. leave the note where it is lying.
D Discuss in groups and write an answer to this question.
Is it possible to open a Morality Shop in your school?
You may discuss the following points / issues:
permission, things / items,
money / fund, how to prevent stealing
